html:
Hul Kuhk'u is the name on the map for an area at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley in California, between today's Bakersfield and the Tehachapi Mountains. Little reliable information about the name itself is available.

This was the land of Southern Valley Yokuts peoples around Buena Vista and Kern lakes, close to the Kitanemuk and the inland Chumash. They fished and gathered tule, acorns and seeds around the lakes and marshes. Spanish missions and, after 1848, the Gold Rush and farming destroyed this world; the lakes were drained for crops.
